_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.native_phrase: font tiếng Việt / font có dấu
phrases.english_concept: Vietnamese-diacritic-safe font/text styling
phrases.content_surface: faq, tool copy, tattoo/caption-style pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to frame a 'will my Vietnamese diacritics survive this style' caveat/FAQ, matching the existing CS-025/HR/SR diacritic-safety pattern. Distinct job from decorative Unicode substitution -- CapCut captions need actual .ttf/.otf font files, not copy-paste glyphs -- flag this mechanism difference if building a CapCut-facing page.

phrases.english_concept: stylish / fancy text generator — the head term for the product category
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, h2, faq, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the primary head term on the vi/ generator surfaces (the vi homepage already does — 'Cách tạo chữ kiểu đẹp trong 3 bước'). 'font chữ đẹp' is a legitimate co-head term and already owns vi/font-chu-dep/; keep the two on their existing pages rather than swapping — this record documents which form means what, it is not a reason to re-target anything.
phrases.good_example: Nhập tên của bạn để tạo chữ kiểu đẹp, copy rồi dán thẳng vào bio.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for the printable/SVG surfaces (bubble-letter sheets, tattoo lettering) — those are not 'chữ kiểu' in the copy-paste sense and a Vietnamese reader will expect a paste target. Do not use in technical/Unicode explanatory copy where 'ký tự Unicode' is the accurate term.

phrases.native_phrase: kí tự đặc biệt (also spelled ký tự đặc biệt)
phrases.english_concept: special characters / decorative symbols to paste into a name or bio
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, h2, faq, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep as the head term for the symbol/character-set surfaces (vi/ki-tu-dac-biet/ and its FF/Liên Quân spokes already do). The useful new guidance is the orthography: use one spelling consistently in the H1/title, and let the other appear naturally once in body/FAQ prose so both forms are represented without keyword-stuffing.
phrases.good_example: Kho kí tự đặc biệt để ghép vào tên nhân vật — bấm là copy.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it as a synonym for 'chữ kiểu' — 'kí tự đặc biệt' is the *pieces* (individual glyphs you assemble), 'chữ kiểu' is the *transform* (your whole word re-rendered). Conflating them is the most common machine-translation tell on Vietnamese competitor pages.

phrases.english_concept: font (as an installable typeface file) — the native word, vs the borrowed 'font'
phrases.content_surface: faq, body prose
phrases.usage_guidance: Use once in body/FAQ prose as the natural synonym so the page does not read as if it only knows the loanword — particularly in the answer explaining that nothing needs to be installed. Keep 'font chữ' in titles/H1s, which is what the target audience types.
phrases.good_example: Bạn không cần tải hay cài phông chữ nào cả — chỉ cần copy rồi dán.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid in gaming-nickname copy (FF, Liên Quân, Roblox) — that audience says 'font' or 'kí tự', and 'phông chữ' reads like a school textbook there. Avoid in a title where 'font chữ đẹp' is the query target.

phrases.native_phrase: copy rồi dán / copy về dán / copy và dán vào
phrases.english_concept: copy and paste (the action) — the everyday form
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, tool copy, button microcopy, step-by-step instructions
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'copy rồi dán' (or 'copy về dán vào …' for the game-name flows) in instructional steps and FAQ answers. Keep 'sao chép' available for the actual button label if a formal register is wanted — competitor tools do exactly this split (button says Sao chép, prose says copy … dán).
phrases.good_example: Chọn kiểu bạn thích, bấm copy rồi dán vào ô đổi tên.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use the loanword form in accessibility, privacy or legal copy, where 'sao chép' is the appropriate register. Do not write 'cóp pi' — see avoid_variants.

phrases.native_phrase: viết không dấu / gõ không dấu / tiếng Việt không dấu
phrases.english_concept: writing/typing Vietnamese without diacritics — the workaround practice AND the search habit
phrases.register: informal practice; the *term* itself is neutral
phrases.content_surface: faq, body prose
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to name the workaround honestly in a diacritic-safety FAQ: a style that cannot carry dấu leaves you writing không dấu, and here is what that costs. Naming it is far better than the machine-translated 'văn bản không có dấu phụ'. It also justifies why the vi/ pages should tolerate unaccented input in the generator without a warning.
phrases.good_example: Nếu kiểu chữ này làm bay hết dấu thì tên của bạn sẽ thành tiếng Việt không dấu — đọc vẫn hiểu, nhưng dễ bị hiểu nhầm.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not recommend it as a solution in a neutral voice — mainstream Vietnamese commentary treats habitual không-dấu writing as sloppy and as a real source of misunderstanding. Present it as a trade-off the user is making, never as the site's advice. Never use unaccented Vietnamese in the site's own headings or UI copy as a 'search optimisation' — that reads as broken Vietnamese to a human.

phrases.native_phrase: lỗi font — hiện ô vuông / ký tự lạ
phrases.english_concept: text renders as empty boxes / garbled characters after pasting
phrases.content_surface: faq (as the question heading), body prose
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the FAQ heading for the 'why does it look wrong on someone else's phone' answer — 'Dán vào thì bị lỗi font, hiện toàn ô vuông thì làm sao?'. Pair with the honest explanation that this is the receiving device lacking the glyph, not the copied text being broken.
phrases.good_example: Dán vào tin nhắn thì bị lỗi font, chữ hiện thành ô vuông.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use this framing for the diacritic-stripping problem (P8) — a Vietnamese reader treats missing dấu and tofu boxes as two different failures, and merging them into one FAQ answer is a translation tell. Avoid 'chữ bị vỡ' in technical copy; it is vivid but imprecise.

phrases.english_concept: the consumable in-game item required to rename your character (rename card)
phrases.content_surface: faq, body prose, tool copy on the game-name pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to frame the check-before-you-commit value proposition on vi/ki-tu-dac-biet-lien-quan/ and vi/ki-tu-dac-biet-ff/ — verify the name fits and is allowed before you spend the thẻ đổi tên. It supports the existing page target; it is not a new page.
phrases.good_example: Kiểm tra tên trước khi dùng thẻ đổi tên — dùng rồi là mất, không hoàn lại.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use on non-gaming pages (Facebook/TikTok/Zalo name changes cost nothing and have no card). Do not state a specific price or currency amount on-page — Garena changes both, and a stale figure is worse than none.

phrases.english_concept: that name is already taken / duplicate name
phrases.content_surface: faq (as the question heading), body prose
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the motivating problem statement on the vi/ game-name pages: your name is trùng, so decorate it. This is the natural Vietnamese framing for why a name generator exists, and it is far stronger than a translated 'tên đã được sử dụng'.
phrases.good_example: Tên bị trùng hoài? Thêm kí tự đặc biệt cho khác đi.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use the player-voice form when quoting or paraphrasing an actual in-game error dialog — reproduce the system wording ('tên này đã được sử dụng') there instead. Not applicable to Facebook/TikTok, where duplicate display names are allowed.

phrases.native_phrase: kí tự khoảng trống / dấu cách tàng hình
phrases.english_concept: invisible/blank Unicode character used to make an empty or oddly-spaced game name
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: The site's existing vi/ky-tu-vo-hinh/ page already carries an H2 'Kí Tự Khoảng Trắng'. The refinement this record adds: in the *gaming* framing the searched noun is 'khoảng trống' (and 'dấu cách'), so game-facing sections and FAQs on that page should use that form, while 'kí tự vô hình' stays correct for the general/technical framing. This is wording guidance on an existing page, not a case for a new one.
phrases.good_example: Copy kí tự khoảng trống rồi dán vào ô đổi tên để tên trông trống.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not promise it works in a specific game — Free Fire has repeatedly blocked specific codepoints across patches, so any claim about which character still works goes stale fast and must be hedged or omitted. Do not use gaming framing on the general Unicode/technical sections.

phrases.english_concept: clan / guild (the group whose name also gets decorated)
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, body prose on the FF page
phrases.usage_guidance: Use on vi/ki-tu-dac-biet-ff/ to cover the group-name job alongside the personal-name job, in the game's own localised vocabulary. Supports that page's existing target; it is not grounds for a separate quân-đoàn page.
phrases.good_example: Kí tự đặc biệt để đặt tên quân đoàn cho cả đội trông đồng bộ.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'quân đoàn' for non-Free-Fire games — say 'bang hội' or 'clan' there. Do not use it in any general/non-gaming copy, where it literally means a military corps.

phrases.english_concept: cool / badass — the dominant aesthetic adjective in VN gaming names
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, body prose, generator example labels
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the aesthetic label on the gaming pages' style groupings ('kiểu chữ ngầu', 'tên ngầu'), and as a category word in generator examples. Supports each game page's existing target; it is a wording choice, not a new segment.
phrases.good_example: Chọn khung ꧁༒꧂ cho tên trông ngầu hơn.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for cute/soft styles — 'ngầu' and 'cute' are opposite poles in Vietnamese and mixing them reads as if the copy does not know what it is describing. Avoid entirely in the printable/practice-sheet, tattoo, accessibility, and privacy copy: it is teen gaming register.

phrases.english_concept: has style / classy in a subtle way — the taste-signalling aesthetic word
phrases.register: informal, broadly used across ages under ~40
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, body prose, generator example labels
phrases.usage_guidance: Use where the appeal is taste rather than aggression — bio styles, minimal/clean styles, the argument for a restrained decorated name. It is the natural bridge word between the gaming pages ('ngầu') and the social/bio pages ('cute'), and it is the one adjective that works on both.
phrases.good_example: Tên ngắn, ít kí tự thôi mà nhìn vẫn chất.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid in explanatory/technical, accessibility, privacy and legal copy — it is evaluative slang and reads as marketing there. Note the homograph trap: 'chất' also means 'substance/material', so avoid it in any sentence about materials, chemicals, or quality-as-durability where the reading flips.

phrases.english_concept: the short profile bio line on Facebook / TikTok / Instagram / Zalo
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, tool copy, usecase pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Use on the vi/ bio and platform usecase surfaces because it matches what the user sees in the app while pasting — matching the app's own Vietnamese UI wording is the highest-value thing localized how-to copy can do. Pair it once with '(bio)' so both search forms are represented naturally.
phrases.good_example: Copy rồi dán vào phần tiểu sử (bio) trên trang cá nhân.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use outside a social-profile context — in general prose 'tiểu sử' means a biography and the sentence will read wrong. Do not use it for a game profile; games use 'hồ sơ' / 'giới thiệu'. Do not state a character limit unless it has been re-verified: the limits reported by Vietnamese sources for the Facebook bio disagree with each other.

phrases.native_phrase: tên hiển thị / tên người dùng
phrases.english_concept: display name vs username — the two different name fields
phrases.content_surface: faq (as the question heading), body prose, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to answer the recurring 'why did my styled name get rejected' question in the audience's own UI vocabulary: it works in tên hiển thị, not in tên người dùng. Gloss the English once in parentheses on first use, exactly as Vietnamese how-to pages do — that gloss is native practice here, not redundancy.
phrases.good_example: Chữ kiểu dán được vào tên hiển thị, còn tên người dùng (@username) thì chỉ nhận chữ và số thường.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not present the accepts/rejects behaviour as a fixed rule per platform — it varies by platform and changes; keep it as a check-your-field explanation rather than a promise. Do not use 'tên hiển thị' for a game character name — that is 'tên nhân vật' (see P14).

phrases.english_concept: name rejected / warned as too long for a game name field
phrases.content_surface: faq
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the VI-locale phrasing for the 'name too long' problem in FAQ/troubleshooting copy. Pairs with VI-025, which supplies the Vietnamese explanation of WHY (capacity, not count).
phrases.good_example: Các bạn không nên tạo tên quá dài vì một số game giới hạn kí tự hiển thị.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for names rejected because a character is banned/filtered — that is a different failure and needs separate VI vocabulary (not yet captured).

phrases.english_concept: styled/special characters consume more of a name limit than plain letters
phrases.content_surface: faq, explainer
phrases.usage_guidance: Use this framing — capacity consumed — when explaining character cost to the VI market, rather than a literal translation of 'counts as two characters'. Conceptual sibling of RU-030 (byte-limit framing) in a different language.
phrases.good_example: Hãy tính toán kỹ vì các kí tự đặc biệt tên FF thường chiếm nhiều dung lượng hơn chữ cái thông thường.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not present as an exact technical rule — the source asserts the direction (special characters cost more) but no VI source found states the actual counting mode, and the per-game mode remains unverified. Do not attach a specific multiplier to this phrase in production copy.

phrases.native_phrase: đếm ký tự / đếm từ / công cụ đếm ký tự
phrases.english_concept: character counter / word counter (the tool category head terms)
phrases.content_surface: page title/H1/meta for a vi counter page
phrases.usage_guidance: Native SERP is crowded with exact-match domains (demkytu.com) and tool pages titled 'Công cụ đếm ký tự online' — 'đếm ký tự' is the unambiguous head term; 'đếm chữ' appears as a secondary variant (trantienduy.com title).
phrases.good_example: Công cụ đếm ký tự online - Đếm từ - Character Count Tool (halink.vn title)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — mainstream utility term

phrases.native_phrase: tin nhắn có dấu / bị tách tin / 70 ký tự
phrases.english_concept: accented Vietnamese SMS counted at 70 chars and split into multiple billed messages
phrases.content_surface: FAQ / explainer section on a vi character-counter page (SMS segment counting)
phrases.usage_guidance: Real, carrier-documented pain: 'có dấu' = 70 chars/segment (UCS-2), 'không dấu' = 160 (GSM-7). A counter that shows SMS segment count for có dấu text serves this directly. Use 'bị tách tin' for the splitting symptom and 'tính tiền' framing for cost.
phrases.good_example: Chúng ta sẽ thấy rất vô lý khi mà viết được khoảng 140 ký tự rồi, lỡ tay gõ một chữ 'à' (thay vì a), thế là tổng số ký tự là 141 (có dấu, và sẽ bị tính tiền là 3 tin nhắn!! (vuhuutiep.wordpress.com)
phrases.avoid_when: not relevant to OTT chat (Zalo/Messenger) copy — SMS-specific

phrases.native_phrase: giới hạn ký tự / Bạn chỉ được nhập tối đa 2000 ký tự
phrases.english_concept: platform post character limit (Zalo's 2000-char post cap as the local anchor case)
phrases.content_surface: platform-limits reference table / FAQ on a vi counter page
phrases.usage_guidance: Zalo is the locally-distinctive limit set no global counter tool documents: 2000-char post cap (verbatim error 'Bạn chỉ được nhập tối đa 2000 ký tự') and the 70-char threshold beyond which Zalo's styled font reverts to default. Use 'giới hạn ký tự' as the generic term.
phrases.good_example: Bài viết Zalo giới hạn 1000 hay 2000 ký tự? Tăng giới hạn được không? (thegioididong.com Q&A title)

phrases.english_concept: "nick" — game ACCOUNT (not display name / nickname styling)
phrases.content_surface: NONE — this is an avoid/de-target signal, not a term to target
phrases.usage_guidance: Do NOT target "nick" queries for name-styling pages. Use "ki tu dac biet" (special characters) or "ten" (name) framing instead — those are the terms that carry the styling intent AND convert.
phrases.good_example: ki tu dac biet Free Fire (correct styling framing) — not "nick FF"
phrases.avoid_when: Never use "nick" as the head term for a display-name/symbol page. First-party GSC proof: vi/usecase/nick-ff/ earns 206 impressions and 1 click (0.49% CTR) because 75%+ of its impressions are navigational queries for competitor ACCOUNT-SHOP domains (nickdep.com 102 imp, khonickff.com, "kho nick ff") — structurally unconvertible for a symbol tool. By contrast VN "ki tu" queries convert at 6-12% CTR (ki tu trai tim 124 imp/9 clk; ki tu discord 76 imp/9 clk).

phrases.english_concept: The game-native VN term for an invisible character; more common in Free Fire / Lien Quan contexts than the literal 'ky t
phrases.content_surface: FAQ; body copy on vi game-name pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FF/LQ gaming context; the more neutral 'ky tu vo hinh' stays correct for general/library copy
phrases.avoid_when: Formal or technical explanatory copy

phrases.english_concept: Dominant VN tool-page and search term; broader than 'invisible' and covers the spacing job as well as the blanking one
phrases.content_surface: page title/H2; FAQ
phrases.usage_guidance: Broadest VN term for this concept — safe as a primary target

phrases.english_concept: Rejection message VN players hit because so many paste the identical invisible string that the resulting name collides
phrases.content_surface: FAQ; troubleshooting copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Explains a failure mode distinct from the character being blocked

phrases.english_concept: The outcome VN players want
phrases.content_surface: FAQ; body copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Loanword-blend; natural in gaming copy only
phrases.avoid_when: Formal copy

phrases.english_concept: to waste a paid rename card for nothing, because the name was rejected
phrases.content_surface: FAQ or answer-page framing only. High emotional charge.
phrases.usage_guidance: FAQ or answer-page framing only. High emotional charge.
phrases.avoid_when: Titles and H1s — the register is too colloquial and complaint-flavoured for a head-term heading; also avoid in any copy that cannot actually back the promise with an accurate per-game check.

phrases.native_phrase: lỗi font / lỗi phông chữ / lỗi font chữ
phrases.english_concept: font/character display error
phrases.content_surface: faq
phrases.usage_guidance: Use only in FAQ/troubleshooting copy explaining why pasted Unicode styles might render as boxes/wrong glyphs on some platforms or fonts — same job as DE's "wird als Kästchen angezeigt" / FR's "s'affiche en carrés", but broader (any display issue, not just boxes). Not a title/H1 term — it is not what someone searches when they want the generator itself.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as a primary head term — it targets a different (troubleshooting) intent than the copy-paste generator queries VI-003/VI-006 own.

phrases.english_concept: dotted/dashed-outline tracing letters (printable format term)
phrases.content_surface: title, h1, faq
phrases.usage_guidance: A format-specific printables term with real independent demand (multiple dedicated sites, standalone font-file downloads like 'UniTapviet_0_ly') — narrower and less consolidated than the generic 'tập viết' term, which established incumbents (Twinkl, Monkey, ILA) already target.

phrases.english_concept: handwriting practice/training
phrases.content_surface: body, faq
phrases.usage_guidance: Parenting-register handwriting-practice vocabulary — pairs with VI-20260814-5uwuj (chữ nét đứt) for a printables/name-tracing content angle.

phrases.english_concept: forum slang: 'easily gets banned'
phrases.content_surface: ready_made_example, none_recommended
phrases.usage_guidance: Flavor/context term for a moderation-risk caution, not a title/H1 term.
